title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia — Supreme Court Defied
description_short: Kilmar Abrego Garcia — Supreme Court Defied
description_medium: The Supreme Court unanimously ordered the Trump administration in April 2025 to facilitate the return of Kilmar Abrego Garcia, a Maryland man who had been illegally deported to El Salvador's CECOT mega-prison despite a standing court order prohibiting his removal. The administration stonewalled, with officials including Stephen Miller and Tom Homan publicly dismissing the Court's authority. As of May 2025, Abrego Garcia remained imprisoned abroad. The case became a symbol of the administration's open defiance of judicial orders.
description_long: In April 2025, the Supreme Court unanimously ordered the Trump administration to facilitate Kilmar Abrego Garcia’s return to the United States. Abrego Garcia, a Maryland resident, had been deported to El Salvador despite a court order prohibiting his removal. The administration’s officials, including Stephen Miller and Tom Homan, publicly disputed or minimized the Court’s authority, while Abrego Garcia remained imprisoned at El Salvador’s CECOT facility as of May. The case tested whether the executive branch would carry out a court order concerning an individual deportation. The Court’s instruction to “facilitate” his return required action by the administration; it did not arrange his return itself. The dispute was therefore about both the original removal and compliance with the remedy ordered by the Court. By May 2025, Abrego Garcia remained in El Salvador; the later outcome is not described. The order addressed Abrego Garcia’s case and did not resolve broader questions about immigration enforcement.
